title.narrative: Conservation of the Archaeological Ruins of Moenjodaro (Pakistan) and Reinforcement of the Disaster Risk Reduction Mechanism

description.narrative:
Conservation of Moenjodaro and Reinforcement of the DRR Mechanism
The Archaeological Ruins at Moenjodaro, a World Heritage site, has long faced significant conservation challenges due to high salinity, humidity, and the impacts of climate change. Building on the legacy of UNESCO’s early international campaign dedicated to this site, a new multi-year technical conservation project aims to tackle these challenges while enhancing preparedness for natural disasters through several key initiatives.
In addition to strengthening technical capacity through both on-site and theoretical training in preventive and remedial conservation, the project’s primary goal is to empower Pakistan’s national stakeholders by enhancing their ability and credibility in managing World Heritage sites and other cultural heritage. It also seeks to renew long-term cooperation at national, regional, and international levels.
Furthermore, the project will serve as a tangible example of integrating disaster risk reduction strategies into the overall management of a renowned World Heritage site. It aims to demonstrate an inclusive and practical approach to addressing the growing risks posed by climate change to earthen architecture and the surrounding environment.
